title: One memory left
takeaway: One real encounter can make you forget everything else.
scene: The beloved looked at the poet only once. That one look changed everything, and then the beloved smiled and walked away.

original: ساقی نظر دے نال کجھ ایسی پلا گیا اے
دل دے صبر قرار نوں دل توں گوا گیا اے
transliteration: Saaqi nazar de naal kujh aisi pila gaya ae
Dil de sabr qaraar nu dil ton gava gaya ae
translation: With a single glance, the saqi poured me such a drink
that my heart lost all its patience and peace.
couplets.story: The saqi, the one who pours, didn't even need a cup. Just one look was enough. It hit him so hard that his heart couldn't stay calm anymore.

original: نیناں چہ آ کے اتھرو طوفان بن گئے نیں
ہاسے اوہ لے گیا اے رونا سکھا گیا اے
transliteration: Nainaan ch aa ke athru toofaan ban gaye nain
Haase oh lai gaya ae, rona sikha gaya ae
translation: Tears came to my eyes and turned into storms.
He took away my laughter and taught me how to cry.
couplets.story: Tears filled his eyes and kept coming like a storm. The beloved took his laughter away and left him knowing only how to cry.

original: اوہ یاد دے گیا اے میں یاد اوہنوں رکھاں
اک یاد اوہدی یاد اے باقی بھلا گیا اے
transliteration: Oh yaad de gaya ae, main yaad ohnu rakhaan
Ik yaad ohdi yaad ae, baaqi bhula gaya ae
translation: He left me with a memory, and I keep remembering him.
Only one memory remains, the memory of him; he made me forget everything else.
couplets.story: The beloved left behind just one thing, a memory, and the poet holds onto it. It's the only thing left in his mind. Everything else is gone.

original: ہُن اوہدے باجھوں مینوں کجھ وی نظر نہ آوے
نظراں دے نال جد دا نظراں ملا گیا اے
transliteration: Hun ohde baajhon mainu kujh vi nazar na aave
Nazraan de naal jad da nazraan mila gaya ae
translation: Now I can see nothing at all except him,
ever since his eyes met mine.
couplets.story: Since their eyes met, he can't see anything else. The beloved fills his whole view.

original: بے ہوش کر گیا اے مکھ توں ہٹا کے پلا
کوہِ طور والی یاد فیر تازہ کرا گیا اے
transliteration: Be-hosh kar gaya ae mukh ton hata ke palla
Koh-e-Toor vaali yaad pher taaza kara gaya ae
translation: He lifted the veil from his face and I fainted.
He brought back the memory of Mount Sinai.
couplets.story: When the beloved lifted the veil and showed their face, the poet passed out. He says it was like what happened at Mount Sinai, when Moses asked to see God and fainted from the light.

original: میں یاد اوہدی اندر بیٹھا ہاں روندا احمدؔ
اوہ مسکرا کے اپنا دامن چھڑا گیا اے
transliteration: Main yaad ohdi andar baitha haan ronda Ahmad
Oh muskura ke apna daaman chhura gaya ae
translation: Ahmad, I sit here weeping, lost in his memory.
He just smiled, pulled his hem from my hand, and left.
couplets.story: Now the poet sits alone, crying and remembering. The beloved didn't stay. They smiled, slipped out of his grip, and walked away.

deeper:
Read this poem next to the story of Moses. In the Qur'an (7:143), Moses asks to see God. God shows Himself to the mountain, the mountain crumbles, and Moses falls unconscious. The poet says the beloved lifting the veil 'brought back the memory of Mount Sinai', which makes it clear the Beloved here is God.

'Only one memory remains, and he made me forget everything else' describes dhikr, the remembrance of God, at its deepest: when remembering Him crowds out everything else. A single glimpse of the divine can leave the seeker in tears for the rest of their life, longing for it to return.
why: It's one of the clearest examples in the book of a love poem that is really about meeting God.
prompt: Is there a moment you keep coming back to in your memory? Why do you think it stuck?
